🚨🇮🇱🇮🇷 A hacked chicken coop camera, Iranian traffic cams Israel used to gather intel before Khamenei was killed, and Russia hacking Ukrainian webcams to aim missile strikes...

There are an estimated 1.2 BILLION internet-connected cameras on earth, and intelligence services now use AI to break into them at scale, turning doorbells and traffic cams into free lookout posts.

-A Chinese-made camera on a chicken coop in northern Israel was hijacked to watch Israeli forces moving along the Lebanon border.

-Israel hacked Iran’s traffic cameras to gather intelligence before the operation that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.

-Iran-linked hackers broke into more than 250 sensitive Israeli cameras this year, including license plate readers and cameras near military outposts.

-A Ukrainian hacker group seized a camera in Crimea, tracked a Russian helicopter and uncovered a secret air base that Ukraine then struck.

-The same group watched cameras on Russia’s Kerch Bridge and spotted motion detectors installed to stop attacks from the water.

-Russian hackers took over webcams in Kyiv to help aim missile strikes, and Ukraine has since secured or blocked roughly 40,000 cameras.

-Dutch intelligence warns Russia is hacking cameras across Europe to track weapons shipments to Ukraine.

So how many cameras near American bases are still running on default passwords?

Every unsecured camera near a base, port or power plant is a GIFT to an enemy, so the cheapest defense in this war is a new password and a software update, and Washington should push that as hard as it pushes interceptors.

Source: The Wall Street Journal / Writer: Daniel
